briefings.title: Kara Swisher Calls Out Elon Musk and Big Tech’s “Petty, Angry" People | Pivot
briefings.channel: Pivot with Kara Swisher and Scott Galloway
briefings.tldr: This briefing covers the passing of media visionary Ted Turner, a mixed earnings week for legacy media giants Disney, Paramount, and Warner Bros. Discovery, and the escalating "petty" legal and corporate drama between Elon Musk and OpenAI.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
This briefing covers the passing of media visionary Ted Turner, a mixed earnings week for legacy media giants Disney, Paramount, and Warner Bros. Discovery, and the escalating "petty" legal and corporate drama between Elon Musk and OpenAI.

## The Legacy of Ted Turner and the Evolution of News
* **A Captain of Industry:** Scott Galloway and Kara Swisher reflect on the death of CNN founder Ted Turner at age 87, describing him as a "different kind of billionaire" who balanced aggressive entrepreneurship with extreme philanthropy.
    * **Key Achievements:** Beyond founding the first 24-hour news cycle, Turner won the America’s Cup and famously donated $1 billion to the United Nations.
    * **Masculinity Role Model:** Galloway highlights Turner as a model for "aspirational masculinity," noting he saw his wealth as an obligation to serve rather than a tool for seeking attention.
* **The Erosion of News Quality:** The speakers trace the decline of news from a money-losing "public service" to a profit-driven "screamfest."
    * **The Murdoch Factor:** Galloway argues that Rupert Murdoch’s insight—that conflict-driven "point/counterpoint" segments drove ratings—eventually led to the hyper-polarized state of modern cable news.

## Media Earnings: Disney Rises While Linear Bleeds
* **Disney’s Momentum:** Under new CEO Josh D'Amaro, Disney reported strong revenue of $25 billion (up 7%). 
    * **Streaming Success:** Streaming operating income jumped 88% to $582 million, with margins hitting double digits (11%) for the first time.
    * **The "Iger" Halo:** Galloway notes that while D’Amaro is at the helm, these results are largely the fruit of Bob Iger’s prior strategic shifts.
* **Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) Struggles:** WBD reported a massive $2.9 billion net loss this quarter.
    * **The "Worst Acquisition" Title:** Galloway suggests Time Warner is the center of the worst value-destruction deals in history (AOL, AT&T, and now WBD).
    * **Linear Decline:** Domestic pay-TV subscribers dropped 10%, highlighting the continued struggle of traditional networks.
* **Paramount’s Resilience:** Paramount beat expectations with $7.35 billion in revenue and added 700,000 subscribers.
    * **Content Strategy:** Despite rumors of "gutting" the studio, Paramount has doubled its film slate for 2026 following the Skydance deal.

## The Musk vs. OpenAI Soap Opera
* **The SpaceX/Anthropic Deal:** Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei reports 80x growth, necessitating a massive compute deal with SpaceX AI (formerly xAI). 
    * **Musk’s About-Face:** After previously calling Anthropic "evil," Musk now claims his "evil detector" wasn't triggered after meeting their executives.
* **The Legal Battle:** Musk’s lawsuit against OpenAI continues to reveal "loathsome" interpersonal drama via court-ordered text releases.
    * **Corporate Infighting:** Testimony from Mira Murati and records involving Shivon Zilis suggest a culture of manipulation and lack of trust, though Swisher and Galloway dismiss most of it as "boring" corporate hijinks rather than illegal activity.
    * **Contract Reality:** Galloway argues Musk has "no legal leg to stand on," characterizing the lawsuit as "seller’s regret" dressed up as a legal argument.

## AI in Finance and Crowdfunding Trends
* **The Limits of AI Investing:** A recent *Wall Street Journal* experiment showed ChatGPT making basic math errors and providing "confident but flawed" investment advice.
    * **The Institutional Gap:** Galloway warns that retail investors using $20/month AI tools are bringing a "squirt gun" to a fight against institutional "howitzers" operated by PhDs at firms like Citadel.
* **Prediction: Crowdfunded Acquisitions:** Galloway predicts that in the next 12–36 months, a charismatic social media figure will successfully crowdfund the acquisition of a small-to-mid-cap company.
    * **Example:** A TikToker recently gathered $132 million in non-binding pledges to try and save Spirit Airlines, indicating a shift in how retail investors might organize via AI and social platforms.

> "These are the richest people on earth and they're so manifestly unhappy. They just can't shut the fuck up... What tiny, petty, angry, unhappy people they all are. Every single one of them."
— **Kara Swisher**

> "Ted Turner saw his wealth and his seat as an obligation... He was optimizing for service, not for attention."
— **Scott Galloway**

> "Every time you place a trade, you gotta keep in mind on the other side of that trade is likely someone smarter than you that has broader technology. The individual... is showing up with a very elegant squirt gun and they have a fucking howitzer."
— **Scott Galloway**

briefings.title: Lyft Earnings Miss Estimates After Global Expansion Push | Bloomberg Intelligence
briefings.tldr: Lyft and travel platforms are navigating a shift toward autonomous vehicle integration and exclusive inventory to combat market saturation, while legacy giants like Intel and Texas Roadhouse leverage strategic alliances and "value-first" branding to drive massive stock recoveries and consumer loyalty.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Lyft and travel platforms are navigating a shift toward autonomous vehicle integration and exclusive inventory to combat market saturation, while legacy giants like Intel and Texas Roadhouse leverage strategic alliances and "value-first" branding to drive massive stock recoveries and consumer loyalty.

## Mobility and Travel: The Shift to Autonomous and Exclusive Supply
* **The Waymo Threat:** Autonomous vehicle (AV) expansion is pressuring the traditional ride-sharing model. Waymo is currently conducting 500,000 rides across more than 10 U.S. cities, nearly doubling its volume over the last 12 months.
    * Both Uber and Lyft are under pressure to move beyond "asset-light" models and add AV capacity to their platforms through partnerships.
* **Lyft’s M&A Potential:** Analysts suggest Lyft could eventually be an acquisition target for platforms like DoorDash.
    * A merger would allow for "agentic AI" use cases and cross-selling opportunities between food delivery and mobility, similar to DoorDash’s expansion in the U.K.
* **Airbnb vs. Expedia:** Airbnb continues to outperform competitors like Expedia due to its "exclusive supply."
    * **Direct Traffic:** Airbnb benefits from being a "verb" in the industry, attracting direct traffic that bypasses expensive marketing channels.
    * **Event Catalysts:** Large-scale events like the FIFA World Cup are expected to be massive demand drivers for the second half of the year across all travel platforms.

## Restaurant Sector: Value Leaders vs. Performance "Disasters"
* **Texas Roadhouse Winning on Volume:** Despite rising beef prices, Texas Roadhouse is seeing strong traffic because of its perceived value.
    * **Trade-Down Trends:** Customers are trading down to cheaper cuts of meat or chicken but are *not* decreasing the frequency of their visits.
* **Wendy’s Momentum Loss:** Described by analysts as a "disaster," Wendy's is struggling to find a turnaround as McDonald’s enters a period of aggressive discounting and the "chicken game" becomes oversaturated.
* **US Foods as a Defensive Play:** The food service distributor is taking market share through a 100% commission-based sales plan and a focus on branded products.
    * **Institutional Stability:** A large portion of their business is tied to "recession-proof" sectors like hospitals, government, and education, where contracts are often indexed to inflation.

## The Cultural Rebirth of Golf and Luxury Branding
* **Audience Expansion:** The U.S. golf audience has surged from 24 million pre-pandemic to 40 million today.
    * The demographic has shifted, becoming younger, more diverse, and highly influenced by social media and "non-traditional" stars from the NBA and NFL.
* **Dewar’s "19th Hole" Strategy:** Luxury brands are moving away from traditional sports sponsorship toward "lifestyle" integration.
    * **Ready-to-Drink (RTD) Innovation:** To attract a younger cohort, Dewar's is focusing on canned cocktails (like the "Lemon Wedge") and partnerships with tech-focused venues like Five Iron Golf and Topgolf.

## Intel’s Strategic Transformation and Political Backing
* **Unprecedented Alliances:** CEO Pat Gelsinger has repositioned Intel as the centerpiece of American manufacturing, securing a 5.5% stake from the U.S. government.
    * Gelsinger has successfully courted industry rivals and partners, including Elon Musk, NVIDIA’s Jensen Huang, and Michael Dell, to support Intel’s CPU role in the AI boom.
* **The "Detail" Challenge:** Despite the stock's massive recent tear (up 460% on a trailing 12-month basis according to the transcript), significant internal work remains.
    * **Manufacturing Quality:** The company must still prove it can fix the quality of its products and factories to move away from outsourcing and regain dominance.
    * **Leadership Style:** Gelsinger’s "venture capital" style of high-level management is a departure from Intel’s historically detail-oriented culture, representing a potential risk.

> "Waymo... is doing 500,000 rides across the U.S. in more than 10 cities. And I think that's where you're starting to see an impact... Uber and Lyft still are growing double digits, but when you look at the take rates, you're starting to see some sort of pressure." — **Mandeep Singh**, Global Tech Research Head, Bloomberg Intelligence

> "Wendy's was a disaster... Discounting is ramping up across the industry. This is the most aggressive I've seen McDonald's in my career. Um, so all of that is going to make the turnaround at Wendy's much more difficult to execute." — **Michael Halen**, Senior Restaurant Analyst, Bloomberg Intelligence

> "He [Pat Gelsinger] has formed an alliance with President Joe Biden. The U.S. is now a major investor in Intel... All of those factors have led to this incredible tear in Intel's stock where it's back to levels we really haven't seen since the dot-com boom." — **Sarah Frier**, Bloomberg Managing Editor

> "It was really the pandemic that grew the built-in audience of golf from around 24 million... to about 40 million today... The profile of the audience has diversified. It's become younger, uh, young adults, much more accessible." — **Brian Cox**, Global VP of Dewar's Scotch Whisky

briefings.title: Marc Lore's Blueprint For Scaling Billion-Dollar Startups

people.name: Marc Lore
people.role: Founder, Chairman, and CEO, Wonder Group

briefings.tldr: Marc Lore is leveraging vertical integration and "physical AI" at Wonder to disrupt the trillion-dollar food industry, utilizing a math-driven scaling framework (VCP) to transition from software-only models to capital-intensive physical infrastructure that creates a defensible market moat.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Marc Lore is leveraging vertical integration and "physical AI" at Wonder to disrupt the trillion-dollar food industry, utilizing a math-driven scaling framework (VCP) to transition from software-only models to capital-intensive physical infrastructure that creates a defensible market moat.

## The Wonder Thesis: "Cloud Kitchens" for the Physical World
* **Vertical Integration:** Lore argues that food delivery aggregators (e.g., DoorDash, Uber Eats) hit a ceiling because they don't own the production. Wonder owns the restaurants, the cooking process, and the delivery to ensure quality and timing.
* **Kitchen as Software:** Wonder is "decoupling the kitchen from the restaurant," similar to how the cloud revolutionized software.
    * **Wonder Create:** A platform launching late 2024 allowing individuals to launch and scale a digital restaurant across Wonder’s infrastructure for $10/month.
* **Operational Density:** A single 2,500-square-foot Wonder kitchen can house 25 different restaurant brands across 20 cuisines (from Bobby Flay steaks to Jose Andres tapas) using electric-only equipment and no open flames.
* **Advanced Logistics:** By owning the tech stack, Wonder sequences cooking so that a multi-restaurant family order finishes simultaneously and is timed perfectly with the courier, resulting in 5-minute average delivery times in urban areas.

## The High-Stakes Pivot: From Vans to Brick-and-Mortar
* **The "Cook-en-Route" Experiment:** Wonder initially utilized 450 Mercedes Sprinter vans to cook food outside customer homes. While customers loved the quality, the model was too capital-intensive and difficult to scale.
* **The Hard Reset:** In early 2023, Lore pivoted the entire company to a brick-and-mortar "hub" model after seeing just three weeks of superior data from a test location.
    * **Financial Impact:** He took a $100M loss and drove revenue to zero to restart with the more scalable model.
    * **Current Trajectory:** Wonder has opened 120 locations in three years; Lore aims to reach 1,000 locations within the next 3.5 years.

## The VCP Framework: Vision, Capital, People
Lore manages his ventures through a proprietary "VCP" system to ensure foundational stability during hyper-growth:
* **Vision:** Writing down a 10–15 year vision and building an organizational structure with **zero dependencies.** Lore hires top-tier leaders and empowers them to run their departments without needing cross-functional approval, which he defines as "true focus."
* **Capital Strategy:** Lore uses a "magic number" (66.66) to determine funding needs based on target valuation.
    * **The Formula:** Divide the target exit valuation by 66.66 to find the necessary seed round. (e.g., To build a $10B company, the seed should be $150M).
    * **The 18-Month Rule:** The goal is to double the company's valuation and the amount of capital raised every 18 months.
* **People & Performance:** Lore emphasizes that investors often over-focus on numbers while ignoring the "foundational systems" of culture and compensation that allow an organization to pivot when things go wrong.

## Automation and "Physical AI" as the New Moat
* **Disrupting Labor Costs:** While e-commerce fights for basis points of margin, restaurants have 30% labor costs ripe for automation.
* **Robotics Integration:** Wonder acquired **Spice Robotics** (an automated bowl-making machine) from Sweetgreen to automate high-volume concepts.
* **Infrastructure as a Moat:** Lore believes capital-intensive businesses are now more attractive than pure software companies because physical infrastructure and proprietary robotics are harder for AI to disintermediate.
* **IPO Goals:** Lore plans to take Wonder public in approximately 11 months to gain access to public currency for further brand acquisitions.

## Notable Quotes

> "We’re doing what the cloud did to software. We’re decoupling the kitchen from the restaurant so that we could scale restaurants like software." — **Marc Lore**

> "I think now with AI... software's become a bad word in the venture community. And here we are... being respected for building a real moat with physical infrastructure and physical AI." — **Marc Lore**

> "Focus is a little bit misunderstood... A lot of it comes down to organizational structure—having the right level person on whatever it is that they're focused on [with no dependencies]." — **Marc Lore**

> "If you have the best people, real clarity around vision, and the right organizational structure that allows people to run and be empowered... magical things will happen." — **Marc Lore**

briefings.title: Marco Rubio BREAKS DOWN America’s GLOBAL GEOPOLITICS in MASTERFUL Press Conference
briefings.tldr: Secretary Marco Rubio emphasized a "U.S. interest first" foreign policy, issuing a stern warning to Iran against seizing international waterways while leveraging the Catholic Church’s global influence to facilitate humanitarian aid in Cuba and Africa.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Secretary Marco Rubio emphasized a "U.S. interest first" foreign policy, issuing a stern warning to Iran against seizing international waterways while leveraging the Catholic Church’s global influence to facilitate humanitarian aid in Cuba and Africa.

## Vatican Relations and Humanitarian Strategy
* **Meeting with Pope Leo:** Secretary Rubio described a "cordial and productive" meeting focused on shared global interests, including the protection of Christian populations in Africa and the Middle East.
    * **Institutional Insights:** Rubio noted that the Church serves as a unique "interlocutor" and information source in regions like Venezuela and Lebanon where U.S. direct access may be limited.
* **Humanitarian Aid in Cuba:** Rubio highlighted the U.S. offer of $100 million in humanitarian aid to Cuba, which he claims the current regime has refused to distribute.
    * **Targeted Sanctions:** He clarified that U.S. sanctions specifically target **GAESA**, a holding company run by Cuban generals, rather than the Cuban people.
    * **The Church’s Role:** The Catholic Church (specifically Caritas) remains the primary vehicle for distributing the $6 million in aid that has successfully reached the island.

## Iran and Maritime Security
* **The "Red Line" on Aggression:** Rubio stated that while "Operation Epic Fear" (the offensive phase) is over, the U.S. will maintain a strictly defensive but lethal posture.
    * **Direct Warning:** Rubio asserted that any Iranian forces threatening U.S. destroyers would be "blown up," regardless of existing "ceasefire" talk.
* **Strait of Hormuz:** Rubio expressed grave concern over reports that Iran is attempting to establish a regulatory agency to control traffic in the straits.
    * **International Precedent:** He warned that "normalizing" a single nation’s control over an international waterway is "unacceptable" and would set a dangerous global precedent.
* **Negotiation Status:** The U.S. is currently awaiting a formal response from Tehran to initiate a serious negotiation process, though Rubio noted the Iranian system remains "fractured and dysfunctional."

## NATO and European Troop Deployments
* **Base Access Friction:** Rubio signaled a potential reassessment of U.S. troop presence based on the cooperation of host nations.
    * **The Spain Example:** He cited instances where NATO allies, specifically Spain, denied the U.S. use of bases during "important contingencies," arguing this undermines the primary logistical reason for a U.S. presence in Europe.
* **Troop Shifting:** He clarified that recent troop withdrawals in Germany (representing less than 14% of the total presence) were "pre-programmed" and merely returned levels to those seen in 2022.
* **National Interest:** Rubio maintained that while he supports NATO, military resources are not unlimited and must be assigned based on current national interests and the stance of member nations toward the U.S.

## Regional Conflicts: Lebanon, Sudan, and Ukraine
* **Lebanon and Hezbollah:** The U.S. goal is to empower the legitimate Lebanese government to confront Hezbollah, which Rubio characterized as a "100 percent Iranian agent" victimizing the Lebanese people. 
* **Sudan Crisis:** Rubio detailed U.S. involvement in the "Quad" process, seeking a humanitarian ceasefire. He accused various third-party countries of using their territories to ship weaponry, turning the conflict into a "proxy engagement."
* **Ukraine Mediation:** Rubio stated that U.S. mediation efforts have "stagnated" but reaffirmed that the U.S. stands ready to facilitate a diplomatic resolution whenever both sides are prepared for a "fruitful outcome."

## Notable Quotes
> "The red line is clear: if they threaten Americans, they're going to get blown up... Only stupid countries don't shoot back when they're shot at, and we're not a stupid country." — **Secretary Marco Rubio**

> "Are you going to normalize a country claiming to control an international waterway? Because if you normalize that, you've set a precedent that's going to get repeated in a dozen other places." — **Secretary Marco Rubio**

> "Hezbollah wouldn't exist without Iran's support... Lebanon should be governed by the Lebanese government; it should not have a terrorist group operating within its national territory." — **Secretary Marco Rubio**

briefings.title: President Donald Trump delivers remarks at the White House — 5/8/2026

briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
President Trump delivered a Mother’s Day address honoring "Angel Moms" and "Gold Star Moms" while highlighting his administration’s claims of achieving zero illegal border crossings, drastic reductions in drug prices, and new financial incentives for American families.

## Border Security and "Angel Moms"
* **Zero Illegal Entries:** The President claimed that for the past 11 months, illegal border crossings have reached "zero," contrasting this with previous "open border" policies that he alleged allowed 25 million people and nearly 12,000 murderers into the country.
* **Angel Moms Recognition:** Trump honored "Angel Moms"—mothers who lost children to crimes committed by undocumented immigrants—specifically naming Mary Ann Mendoza, Tammy Nobles, and Jacqueline Medina.
* **Policy Shift:** He attributed the lack of current crossings to a shift in messaging and enforcement, stating that migrants no longer attempt the journey because they know "they’re not going to get through."

## Drug Epidemic and Interdiction
* **Supply Reductions:** Reported that fentanyl flow across the border is down by 59%, while illegal drugs entering by sea have dropped by 97%.
* **HALT Fentanyl Act:** Highlighted the signing of the HALT Fentanyl Act as a primary tool in stopping the "poison" that causes an estimated 200,000 American deaths annually.
* **Cartel Influence:** Noted that while the sea routes are largely secured, land routes remain a challenge due to Mexican cartels "ruling" the region.

## Gold Star Families and Military Remembrance
* **Abbey Gate Tribute:** Trump honored mothers of service members killed during the 2021 Abbey Gate attack in Afghanistan, including Alicia Lopez and Paula Knauss Selph, while criticizing the previous administration for "gross incompetence" regarding the withdrawal.
* **Marine Captain Jesse Melton:** Shared the story of Captain Melton, who died in Afghanistan in 2008 after volunteering to take a fellow Marine's place so his comrade could be present for his daughter's birth.
* **Administration Personnel:** Recognized female leaders within his administration, including Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins and Chief of Staff Susie Wiles.

## Economic and Social Policy for Families
* **Newborn Investment Grants:** Announced a policy giving every American newborn $1,000 to invest for their future, bolstered by a $6.25 billion contribution from the Dell family.
* **Family Financial Support:** 
    * **Tax Credits:** Cited the expansion of the Child Tax Credit to $2,200 per child.
    * **"Trump Accounts":** Introduced tax-advantaged savings accounts to help families save for their children's futures.
    * **Healthcare:** Claimed a 70–90% reduction in prescription drug prices by implementing "Most Favored Nations" pricing, ensuring the U.S. pays the lowest global price.
* **Social Stance:** Reaffirmed his administration's commitment to school choice, keeping biological men out of women's sports, and banning "transgender mutilation" of children.

## Rose Garden and White House Renovations
* **Infrastructure Improvements:** Described the renovation of the Rose Garden, replacing grass (which was often muddy due to the area being a wetland) with white stone and black granite to accommodate events and media.
* **Presidential Walk of Fame:** Highlighted a new installation featuring portraits of U.S. Presidents from George Washington to the present.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "In securing our border we've also made tremendous strides in stopping the flow of illegal drugs into our country, the flood of deadly fentanyl across our border is down by 59 percent and the drugs coming in by sea are down by 97 percent."
— **President Donald Trump**

> "We are giving every American newborn child $1,000 automatically to invest and to grow over the course of their life."
— **President Donald Trump**

> "For 28 years drug prices and prescription drugs only went in one direction... Now we have the lowest drug prices in the world... we cut them by 50, 60, 70 percent."
— **President Donald Trump**

briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
President Trump hosted a Rose Garden event to honor Mother’s Day, specifically recognizing "Angel Moms" and Gold Star families while highlighting administration successes in border security, drug price reduction, and family-focused economic incentives.

## Border Security and "Angel Moms"
The President dedicated a significant portion of his remarks to mothers whose children were victims of crimes committed by illegal immigrants, linking their loss to national security policy.

*   **Zero-Tolerance Results:** Trump claimed that the southern border has achieved "zero" illegal crossings over the last 11 months, attributing this to a shift from "open border" policies to the "strongest border in American history."
*   **Angel Mom Recognition:** He specifically recognized Mary Ann Mendoza, Tammy Nobles, and Jacqueline Medina, praising their "unyielding resolve" in advocating for stricter immigration enforcement to prevent further tragedies.
*   **Criminal Statistics:** The President stated that 11,888 murderers had previously been allowed into the country under prior administrations and claimed that his administration is actively removing these individuals.

## Fentanyl and the Drug Epidemic
The briefing detailed progress in the "war on drugs," focusing on the reduction of synthetic opioids entering the United States.

*   **Supply Chain Disruptions:**
    *   **Maritime Interdiction:** Reported a 97% decrease in illegal drugs entering the country by sea.
    *   **Fentanyl Reduction:** Claimed a 59% drop in the flow of fentanyl across land borders.
*   **Legislative Action:** Trump highlighted the signing of the **HALT Fentanyl Act** as a cornerstone of his mission to end the drug epidemic.
*   **Cartel Influence:** Acknowledged the difficulty of land enforcement due to the power of Mexican cartels, noting that "poison" still claims roughly 200,000 American lives annually.

## Military Sacrifice and Gold Star Honors
The President paid tribute to mothers of fallen service members, focusing on the human cost of military engagement and recent tactical failures.

*   **The Story of Jesse Melton:** Trump honored Gold Star Mom Janice Chance, recounting the story of Marine Captain Jesse Melton, who volunteered to take a comrade's place so the fellow Marine could witness his daughter's birth, ultimately losing his life.
*   **Abbey Gate Criticism:** He specifically addressed mothers of those killed during the Afghanistan withdrawal at Abbey Gate, calling the event a result of "gross incompetence" by the previous administration.
*   **Gold Star Mothers Present:** Recognized Alice Lopez, Alicia Lopez, Paula Knauss-Self, and Coral Darsino for their sacrifice and resilience.

## Family Economic Policy and Healthcare
The President outlined a series of financial incentives designed to support American families and lower the cost of living.

*   **Direct Financial Support:**
    *   **Newborn Grants:** Announced a program giving every American newborn $1,000 automatically for long-term investment.
    *   **Trump Accounts:** Tax-advantaged savings accounts designed to help families save for their children's futures.
    *   **Child Tax Credit:** Highlighted the expansion of the credit to $2,200 per child.
*   **Healthcare Costs:**
    *   **Prescription Drugs:** Claimed a 70–90% reduction in drug prices through a "most favored nations" policy, ensuring the U.S. pays the lowest price globally for prescriptions.
    *   **Family Planning:** Pledged to lower the costs of IVF and cut regulatory barriers for families.
*   **Education:** Ttouted the "largest expansion of school choice in American history."

## Rose Garden Renovations
Trump opened the event by discussing the physical transformation of the Rose Garden and the White House grounds.

*   **Structural Upgrades:** Replaced the "wetland" grass with white stone to prevent mud and allow for year-round events, such as lunches and news conferences.
*   **Presidential Walk of Fame:** Introduced a new installation featuring black granite and images of U.S. presidents from George Washington to the present.

> "In their honor, we’ve rapidly turned the worst and most dangerous border in the history of our country into the strongest border in American history... during the last 11 months, we have zero, zero [crossings]." — **President Donald J. Trump**

> "We had the highest drug prices in the world by far; now we have the lowest drug prices in the world... Drugs that were costing in London $10 for a pill would cost $130 for a pill in the United States, and now... that’s what we pay." — **President Donald J. Trump**

> "America is a strong and free nation today because of people like your great son [Jesse Melton] and we want to thank you for being here." — **President Donald J. Trump** to Gold Star Mom Janice Chance

briefings.title: Raising Cane's CEO Todd Graves: Building a billion-dollar brand on one menu item | Masters of Scale
briefings.tldr: Todd Graves built Raising Cane’s into a multi-billion-dollar empire by defying industry norms, maintaining a strict focus on a limited menu, and prioritizing long-term cultural integrity over short-term private equity gains.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Todd Graves built Raising Cane’s into a multi-billion-dollar empire by defying industry norms, maintaining a strict focus on a limited menu, and prioritizing long-term cultural integrity over short-term private equity gains. His journey from working as an Alaskan fisherman to fund his first location highlights a "never quit" mentality that remains the brand’s core driver.

## The Founding Philosophy: Simplicity as a Competitive Edge
* **The "B-Minus" Business Plan:** While in college ('90–'94), Graves wrote a business plan for a chicken finger restaurant that received the lowest grade in the class.
    * **Industry Pushback:** The professor argued the plan ignored the industry trend toward variety (e.g., McDonald’s adding salads and wraps) to avoid the "veto vote."
    * **Graves’ Counter-Intuition:** He believed that executing one thing better than anyone else would create a "craveable" destination. He cited In-N-Out Burger (founded in 1948) as an eventual model for this focused approach.
* **Operational Efficiency:** The limited menu allows for "scratch cooking" and high-speed service.
    * **Speed Factors:** Customers don’t need to study the menu; they often order by name (e.g., "Box Combo, no slaw, extra toast"). 
    * **Consistency:** By refusing to add items like spicy chicken or barbecue sauce, the kitchens maintain specialized, high-speed cooking procedures that "seconds matter" in the drive-thru.

## Funding Through Grit and Manual Labor
* **Bootstrapping the Vision:** After being rejected by every bank in town, Graves committed to funding the restaurant himself through grueling manual labor.
    * **Boilermaker Work:** He worked 90-hour weeks in California oil refineries (El Segundo and Torrance) to accumulate capital.
    * **Alaskan Fishing:** On the advice of a coworker, "Wild Bill" Tolar, Graves spent a summer in Naknek, Alaska, gillnetting sockeye salmon. He worked 20-hour days with only four hours of fragmented sleep to save the final $40,000–$60,000 needed.
* **The First Location:** Graves opened the first Raising Cane’s at the north gates of LSU in a dilapidated building he renovated himself to save costs, learning plumbing and contracting on the job.

## Ownership Strategy: Eschewing Franchises and Private Equity
* **Shift to Company-Owned:** Graves originally planned for a 60/40 split between company-owned and franchised locations but eventually bought back his franchisees.
    * **The Excellence Gap:** He noted that while his company-owned stores operated at a 95/100 level, even good franchisees hovered around 85/100. This 10% difference in quality and culture drove him to move to a 100% company-operated model.
* **The "Death by a Thousand Cuts" Warning:** Graves strongly advises founders against selling to private equity firms that prioritize three-to-five-year exit strategies.
    * **Boardroom Erosion:** He argues that PE-backed companies often make small, incremental cuts—like cheaper music systems or commissary-made sauce—that destroy crew morale and product quality over time.
    * **Purpose-Driven Growth:** Graves views his success as a platform to help his crew and community, a mission he believes is often lost when shareholders prioritize quarterly financial returns.

## Marketing through "Caneiac" Culture
* **Top-of-Mind Awareness:** Graves emphasizes the need to be visible the moment a customer asks, "What do we want for lunch?" This is achieved through heavy investment in billboards, radio, and timely TV placements.
* **Authentic Celebrity Partnerships:** The brand utilizes "celebrity Caneiacs" who genuinely love the food, such as Snoop Dogg, Saquon Barkley, and Cynthia Erivo.
    * **Humanizing the Brand:** Marketing stunts, such as Snoop Dogg working a drive-thru window or hosting a fashion show during Fashion Week, keep the brand relevant and "cool" without taking itself too seriously.
* **Personal Leadership:** Graves models himself after founders like Dave Thomas (Wendy’s), believing that a visible founder conveys a commitment to food safety and quality that a faceless corporation cannot.

## Future Outlook: AI and Human Connection
* **AI for Prediction, Not Replacement:** Raising Cane’s uses AI for data compilation and drive-thru speed optimization but Graves is hesitant to replace staff with robotics.
* **The Human Advantage:** Graves believes that as competitors move toward fully robotic restaurants, Raising Cane’s "human touch"—friendly crew and handmade food—will become an even stronger competitive differentiator.

***

> "The subconscious believes what you tell it... You can get up in the morning and say, 'Hey, I'm going to have a great day,' or you can get up and go, 'Oh my God, it's just going to be a tough day.' And whatever you say is pretty much right." — **Todd Graves**

> "If you're sitting in a boardroom and the CFO says, 'Here's 15 things I can cut to make us more profitable'... it’s death by a thousand cuts. You implement it from a boardroom without being in the kitchens, and you lose the crew's attitude and the customer service." — **Todd Graves**

> "If you try to be all things to all people, you're not serving any of them well." — **Todd Graves**

briefings.title: S&P Hits New Highs as Tech Earnings Crush Recession Fears | The Weekly Wrap
briefings.tldr: Despite geopolitical tensions in Iran and elevated valuations, the S&P 500 continues to hit new highs because all 11 sectors are beating revenue estimates and profit margins have reached an all-time high of 20%.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** (1-2 sentences): Despite geopolitical tensions in Iran and elevated valuations, the S&P 500 continues to hit new highs because all 11 sectors are beating revenue estimates and profit margins have reached an all-time high of 20%. The market is currently "K-shaped," driven upward by dominant tech, industrial power, and financial sectors while the lower-end consumer and software-specific stocks struggle.

## Macroeconomic Health & The "K-Shaped" Reality
* **Recession Indicators:** Steve Eisman argues that a recession is not imminent because revenue and earnings growth continue to exceed analyst expectations across the board.
    * **Revenue Growth:** Actual S&P 500 revenue growth reached 10.5% for Q1 2026, significantly higher than the 7.5% predicted at the start of the year.
    * **Margin Expansion:** S&P 500 operating margins are at a record 20%, up from 16% in 2023. Eisman notes it is difficult to be bearish when margins expand alongside revenue.
* **The K-Shaped Economy:** Market strength is concentrated in specific "upward" sectors while others languish.
    * **The "Up" Side:** Led by Tech, Industrials related to power, and Financials.
    * **The "Down" Side:** Middle to lower-end consumers are struggling, and the housing market remains "effectively flat."
* **Market Concentration:** Info Tech now represents 35% of the S&P 500; when adding tech-adjacent firms like Google, Meta, and Amazon, the total reaches nearly 50%. This concentration means the index can rise as long as tech performs, even if the broader consumer environment is weak.

## Tech Performance: Hardware Wins, Software Struggles
* **AI Hardware Strength:** Companies building the infrastructure for AI continue to report massive growth.
    * **AMD:** Reported Q1 sales growth of 38% and projected strong Q2 sales of $11.2 billion, sending the stock up 15%.
    * **Arista Networks:** Posted a 34% increase in EPS, though the stock cooled due to high prior valuations.
    * **Rockwell Automation:** Reported a strong beat with 9% organic sales growth, benefiting from the build-out of AI data centers.
* **The "Software Problem":** Despite strong numbers, software stocks are being punished by "AI fears" and valuation resets.
    * **Palantir:** Revenue grew 85% and EPS rose 154%, yet the stock remained pressured by a negative AI narrative.
    * **Shopify:** Down over 30% YTD due to slowing revenue guidance and general software sector malaise.
* **Payment Sector Volatility:** Competition is intensifying as Apple and Google Pay erode traditional players.
    * **PayPal & Fiserv:** Both companies reported poor guidance and organic growth issues; Eisman views Visa and Mastercard as the only "impregnable" franchises in the space.

## Logistics, Energy, & Corporate Disruptions
* **Amazon vs. The World:** Amazon is opening its internal distribution network to non-Amazon sellers, directly competing with FedEx and UPS in freight and parcel shipping.
* **The GameStop/eBay Bid:** GameStop made a surprise $60 billion bid for eBay (a company four times its size). 
    * **Expert Reaction:** Eisman expects eBay to reject the deal; notably, Michael Burry sold his entire GameStop position following the news due to concerns over debt levels.
* **Energy & Geopolitics:** Oil prices surged following attacks in the Strait of Hormuz but settled below $100 as the market adopted a "glass half-full" view of the Iran conflict.
    * **Diamondback Energy:** Increased production targets due to higher prices, with EPS expected to grow over 100% in Q2.

## Financials & Private Credit Risks
* **Apollo’s Transparency Move:** In a major industry shift, Apollo announced it will provide daily pricing for its investment-grade corporate fixed income and direct lending assets by September.
* **Private Equity Warning:** Eisman remains concerned about private equity's overexposure to software. 
    * **Valuation Gap:** With public software stocks down significantly, many private companies may be worth half of their original investment, potentially forcing lenders to demand more equity.
* **FICO Controversy:** Eisman highlighted a 1,500% increase in the price of FICO reports over the last five years, calling it one of the most "egregious monopolistic acts" in the lending ecosystem.

## Notable Quotes
> "The overall story, in my view, continues to be a K-shaped market, reflecting the underlying K-shaped economy... As the lower part of the K spending shrinks, the percentage impact on the S&P shrinks because tech dominates the S&P to an incredible degree." — **Steve Eisman**

> "It's more difficult to take a negative view on the economic outlook when margins are expanding with revenue." — **Steve Eisman**

> "Anything, anything in software is problematic because of AI fears... even though the company reported mostly a good quarter, the negative AI narrative still dominates." — **Steve Eisman** (on Palantir and Shopify)

> "The most important statement I can make about Disney is that the stock price is where it was 10 years ago." — **Steve Eisman**

briefings.title: Secretary of State Rubio Speaks to Reporters in Rome
briefings.tldr: Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s visit to Rome focused on aligning with the Vatican and the Italian government on global security threats, specifically Iran’s maritime aggression and the need for humanitarian corridors in Cuba and Sudan.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s visit to Rome focused on aligning with the Vatican and the Italian government on global security threats, specifically Iran’s maritime aggression and the need for humanitarian corridors in Cuba and Sudan. Rubio reaffirmed that while the U.S. remains committed to NATO, future troop deployments will be contingent on members' willingness to grant the U.S. logistical power projection during global contingencies.

## Diplomatic Engagement with the Vatican
* **The Papal Meeting:** Rubio characterized his meeting with Pope Leo as "cordial and important," focusing on the Church’s role as a global spiritual leader and humanitarian facilitator.
    * **Strategic Alignment:** Discussions covered Christian populations in Africa, the situation in Lebanon, and the Church’s insights into Latin American political dynamics.
    * **Addressing Tension:** Rubio dismissed media narratives regarding President Trump’s past criticisms of the Pope, stating the President will act in the U.S. interest while maintaining a "productive and fruitful" relationship with the Church.
* **Humanitarian Aid to Cuba:** Rubio highlighted that the U.S. has offered $100 million in humanitarian aid to the Cuban people, but the "incompetent regime" is blocking distribution.
    * **Role of the Church:** The Catholic agency Caritas remains a primary partner for distributing aid, such as recent hurricane relief.

## National Security and NATO Strategy
* **NATO and Troop Presence:** Rubio addressed potential U.S. troop withdrawals from Europe, noting that while no final decisions have been made by the President, the U.S. is reassessing its footprint.
    * **Base Access Challenges:** Rubio expressed frustration with NATO allies—specifically citing Spain—who denied the U.S. use of bases during recent "contingencies." 
    * **Policy Shift:** He warned that if NATO membership no longer guarantees the ability to project power from European bases, the U.S. must examine the cost and utility of those deployments.
* **Ukraine and Russia:** Rubio described the ongoing conflict as a tragedy and noted that U.S. mediation efforts have "stagnated." He emphasized that the U.S. stands ready to mediate only if there is a realistic opportunity for a diplomatic resolution.

## Iranian Aggression and International Waterways
* **Maritime "Red Lines":** Rubio warned that Iran is attempting to "normalize" illegal control over international waterways, specifically the Strait of Hormuz.
    * **Defensive Posture:** Following reports of U.S. destroyers being fired upon, Rubio stated that any threat to American assets would be met with immediate force. 
    * **Operation Epic Fury:** He distinguished current defensive responses from "Operation Epic Fury," which he defined as a completed offensive mission that successfully destroyed Iranian missile launchers and air capabilities.
* **Nuclear Ambitions:** Rubio asserted there is global consensus that a nuclear-armed Iran is "unacceptable," but emphasized that the current administration is the first to take "concrete" action to prevent it.

## Regional Conflicts and Foreign Policy
* **Lebanon and Hezbollah:** The U.S. goal is a strong Lebanese government capable of confronting Hezbollah. Rubio called on Italy to play a role in equipping the Lebanese military and cutting off illicit financing for the Iranian-backed group.
* **Sudan Crisis:** Rubio identified Sudan as one of the world's worst humanitarian crises. The U.S. is pushing for a "humanitarian ceasefire" and safe havens for aid distribution through the "quad process."
* **Cuba Sanctions:** Rubio clarified that recent sanctions target **GAESA**, a holding company run by Cuban generals that "steals from the Cuban people" to enrich regime insiders, rather than targeting the populace directly.
* **Taiwan:** Ahead of a scheduled trip to China, Rubio reaffirmed that U.S. policy remains unchanged: the U.S. opposes any forced or compelled change to the status quo in the Taiwan Strait.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "The red line is clear: if they threaten Americans they're going to get blown up... If you fire a missile at the United States and we saw you fire it, we're going to hit you. Of course we are. Who doesn't do that?" — **Secretary of State Marco Rubio**

> "One of the advantages of being in NATO is that it allows us to have forces deployed in Europe... some countries in Europe, like Spain as an example, denied us the use of those bases for a very important contingency... if that's no longer the case... that's a problem and it has to be examined." — **Secretary of State Marco Rubio**

> "We have the most resources, but our resources are not unlimited. We have to always assign resources around the world including military resources on the basis of what serves the national interest." — **Secretary of State Marco Rubio**

briefings.title: The Right After Trump (Ft. Benjamin Teitelbaum)
briefings.tldr: The contemporary far-right is a fractured coalition of "Traditionalists" seeking to restore a structured past and "Futurists" pursuing a borderless, tech-driven hierarchy.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The contemporary far-right is a fractured coalition of "Traditionalists" seeking to restore a structured past and "Futurists" pursuing a borderless, tech-driven hierarchy. Understanding these movements requires moving beyond the "fascism" label to analyze their specific anti-liberal philosophies and the novel strategies they use to challenge mainstream democracy.

## Ethnography and the "Deep Hanging Out" Method
* **The Ethnographic Approach:** Professor Benjamin Teitelbaum utilizes "deep hanging out"—a form of long-term immersive research—to understand far-right actors as people rather than just studying their texts or music. 
    * This method seeks a "knowledge of someone that comes when you know them well" through formal interviews and informal social interaction.
* **Critique of "Activist Scholarship":** Teitelbaum distinguishes his work from "activist scholars" who enter research with pre-determined political conclusions. 
    * He argues that starting a project with the intent to combat the subject prevents true understanding, as the researcher is no longer open to learning unexpected insights.
* **Mainstreaming of the Fringe:** Teitelbaum notes that groups like the Sweden Democrats moved from the radical margins to the center of national politics, meaning that to study the far-right today is to study the state of Western society as a whole.

## The Ideology of Steve Bannon and "Traditionalism"
* **Bannon as a Contradiction:** Teitelbaum describes Bannon as an "American nationalist anti-liberal." 
    * He attempts to fuse the American revolutionary spirit (which is forward-looking and emancipatory) with "Capital T" Traditionalism (which is backward-looking and focuses on inherited identity).
* **Capital "T" Traditionalism:** This philosophical school, rooted in the work of René Guénon, posits that a "true religion" existed in the past but has been degraded over time.
    * **Cyclic Time:** Traditionalists reject linear progress, believing instead in a cycle of decline from a Golden Age to a Dark Age (the Hindu "Kali Yuga").
    * **Hierarchy and Borders:** They believe a virtuous society requires rigid structure and caste-like hierarchies. A "Dark Age" is defined by borderlessness, intermixing, and the triumph of materialism over spirituality.
* **The "Legacy American" Focus:** While Bannon has recently reached out to the Black working class for electoral reasons, his core philosophy prioritizes "legacy Americans"—those whose families participated in the historical construction of the U.S. state.

## Geopolitical Tensions: Bannon vs. Alexander Dugin
* **Civilizational Disagreement:** While Bannon and Russian philosopher Alexander Dugin both hate globalist liberalism, they disagree on the role of the United States.
    * Dugin views the U.S. as the "purest embodiment" of the disease of liberalism.
    * Bannon argues for a "tribal Americanism" that is inherently Christian and nationalist, suggesting the U.S. and Russia should be allies against non-Christian powers.
* **The China/Iran Divide:** The collaboration between Bannon and Dugin collapsed over other nations. 
    * **Bannon’s View:** Wants a global alliance of Christian nations to exclude China and Iran.
    * **Dugin’s View:** A religious pluralist who values theocracy over democracy; he views Iran as a natural ally because it prioritizes the "spiritual and eternal" over liberal materialism.

## The Future: Traditionalist Right vs. Futurist Right
* **The Tech-Right Schism:** A major rift exists between Bannon’s "nostalgic reactionary right" and the "futurist right" (represented by figures like Peter Thiel and Elon Musk).
    * **Nostalgic Right:** Focuses on "Make America Great *Again*," seeking to restore order through historical models.
    * **Futurist Right:** Seeks a "future arrived early," characterized by the disintegration of inherited social orders and a hierarchy based on technological performance rather than tradition.
* **Disavowal of Democracy:** Both factions are united by a skepticism of democracy, though for different reasons. Bannon wants archaic, "non-bureaucratized" communities, while the Tech-Right views democracy as an inefficient process that is "100% dispensable" if it fails to deliver specific products or outcomes.

## Re-evaluating the "Fascism" Label
* **The Problem with "Crying Fascism":** Teitelbaum argues the term "fascist" is often used as a tool to exclude people from political life rather than to describe them accurately.
    * **De-stigmatization:** Overusing the label can lead to "ironic" embrace or nihilism among young right-wingers, such as Nick Fuentes, who use taboo-breaking as a communication strategy.
* **Focus on Novelties over Redundancies:** Teitelbaum warns that labeling figures like Bannon as "fascists" suggests we already understand them perfectly because we have seen fascism before.
    * He insists that the most important things to learn about the contemporary radical right are its *novelties*—the ways it defies historical rules and anticipates a future that opponents are not prepared for.

***

> "It is a lost dream and it should be an abandoned dream of the opponents of the far-right that they're just going to vanquish their enemies... I think that politics have been transformed." — **Benjamin Teitelbaum**

> "Americanism is a tribalism. And that tribalism, Bannon said, not only is- are there links between it and Russia and Russian tribalism, but it's very much as part of this anti-liberal lifeway." — **Benjamin Teitelbaum**

> "I believe that the most important things to learn and to understand about the contemporary radical right are its novelties, not its redundancies... The novelties are what we don't want to face up to." — **Benjamin Teitelbaum**

briefings.title: Thin Harness, Fat Skills: The New Way To Build Software
briefings.tldr: AI agents have transitioned software development from a manual "writing" task to a high-leverage "director" role, enabling founders to achieve a 400x increase in output by "tokenmaxxing" and utilizing agentic workflows.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
AI agents have transitioned software development from a manual "writing" task to a high-leverage "director" role, enabling founders to achieve a 400x increase in output by "tokenmaxxing" and utilizing agentic workflows.

## The Return of the Builder: Garry Tan’s 400x Productivity Leap
* **The Comeback:** After a 13-year hiatus from active coding, YC CEO Garry Tan returned to building software, shipping hundreds of thousands of lines of code and launching viral open-source projects like *gstack*.
* **Cost and Velocity Collapse:** 
    * In 2008, building a blogging platform (Posterous) took $4M and 1.5 years.
    * In 2024, rebuilding a more advanced version with agentic research capabilities took $200 in tokens and 5 days.
* **The 400x Output Metric:** Tan calculated that by directing 15 agents simultaneously, his logical lines of code (LLOC) production is 400 times higher than his peak output in 2013.
* **The Ferrari Analogy:** Tan describes using modern AI agents as "driving a Ferrari"—exhilarating and incredibly fast, but requiring the user to be a "mechanic" who can pop the hood and fix the system when it breaks down.

## "Tokenmaxxing" and Agentic Engineering
* **Defining Tokenmaxxing:** The philosophy of intentionally spending heavily on high-quality model calls (e.g., $500/day) to "boil the ocean" of research, context, and testing. 
* **Journalistic Software:** Tan's project *Garry’s List* acts as an investigative journalist rather than just a CMS. It uses APIs (Perplexity, X, Grok) to ingest dozens of sources, cross-reference arguments, and produce sourced reports.
* **Latent Space vs. Deterministic Code:** Success in AI engineering depends on knowing which tasks belong in "LLM land" (handling generic cases, user intent) and which belong in "code land" (deterministic logic).
* **The "Rent" Mental Model:** Spending on tokens should be viewed like San Francisco rent for a startup—it is an expensive but necessary investment to create the serendipity and utility required for high-speed growth.

## The gstack Workflow: Thin Harness, Fat Skills
* **Thin Harness:** The core loop that manages LLM inputs/outputs and tool calls (e.g., Claude Code). 
* **Fat Skills:** The high-quality markdown, prompts, and logical checklists supplied by the human "director" to guide the agent.
* **The Multi-Stage Pipeline:** Tan uses a specific sequence of "skills" to ensure code quality:
    * **ASCII Visualization:** Forcing the AI to create data flow diagrams before coding to ensure it understands the architecture.
    * **The CEO Skill:** A meta-prompt inspired by Brian Chesky’s "10-star experience" that asks the AI to find a path to 10x value for only 2x effort.
    * **The Eng Review:** Automating the creation of unit and integration tests, reaching 80-90% coverage—a task human developers often neglect.
    * **Codex/QA:** Using high-IQ models to find bugs and Playwright-wrapped agents to perform automated browser-based testing of UIs.

## The Future of Personal AI and Human Agency
* **Personal vs. Corporate AI:** Tan argues the defining question of the era is whether individuals will control their own tools and data or be controlled by corporate-hosted algorithms (similar to a Facebook feed).
* **Open Source Golden Age:** Using tools like *Conductor* and *G Brain*, developers can now "extract" logic from existing repos and use AI to build complex RAG systems in a single weekend.
* **The AI Time Dividend:** AI allows busy executives to "buy back time" by utilizing machine consciousness to handle the "boring" parts of engineering (QA, boilerplate, research), leaving humans to provide taste and product intuition.

> "Using OpenClaude these days is like driving a Ferrari... it’s exhilarating. It figures things out you would never think a machine could figure out... But then it's also like a Ferrari in that you better be a mechanic. You’re going to have to fix it yourself." — **Garry Tan**

> "If you can tokenmax, it’s like... you could buy millions of years of consciousness, of machine consciousness. Now I can be a time billionaire. It’s not my own time; it’s the time of a machine doing work for me." — **Garry Tan**

> "Markdown is actually code; it’s just compiled in a different way. You can get the computer to do really astonishing things... I don’t use Visual Studio at all. There’s no reason to when I can talk to my agent." — **Garry Tan**

briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The ongoing conflict with Iran and sustained high energy prices present significant political risks for incumbents ahead of the midterms, while the domestic debate shifts toward "Gilded Age" inequality and the role of state intervention in the economy.

## Iran Conflict and Economic Stability
* **Market Resilience:** Despite geopolitical chaos, markets have remained surprisingly stable. Heidi Heitkamp attributes this to the underlying strength and innovation of the American worker, though she warns the **$40 trillion national debt** remains a looming "wildcard."
* **Policy Inconsistency:** Heitkamp notes a lack of consistency in war execution, which is creating anxiety in "farm country" due to skyrocketing fertilizer costs and diesel prices.
* **The "Success" Metric:** Mick Mulvaney defines Republican success as a total end to the Iranian nuclear program and ensuring the **Straits of Hormuz** remain permanently open. He argues Trump cannot exit the conflict until these conditions are met, as a closed strait is an unacceptable economic loss.

## Midterm Election Pressure
* **Gas Price Vulnerability:** Both speakers agree that $4.50 per gallon gas entering the August/September window is a "tough sell" for the incumbent party.
* **Managing Expectations:** President Trump has reportedly begun setting expectations that gas prices will not drop significantly before the midterms, avoiding promises he cannot keep.
* **The "Boots on the Ground" Risk:** Heitkamp suggests that eliminating enriched Iranian material may require a ground invasion—a move that would trigger a massive backlash from isolationist voters.

## Structural Energy Challenges
* **Slow Recovery:** Experts warn that reopening the Straits will not act as a "light switch" for the economy. It could take 4–5 months to see price relief.
* **Supply Deficit:** **10% to 15% of Qatari gas production** is currently offline and may remain so for several years, representing structural damage that cannot be quickly repaired.
* **The "Nacho" Concept:** Mulvaney dismissed the "nacho" theory (the idea that the Strait of Hormuz may never fully reopen), stating the U.S. economy simply cannot tolerate that outcome.

## Domestic Political Tensions: Mamdani vs. Griffin
* **Class Warfare:** The public dispute between NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani and billionaire Ken Griffin reflects a broader "Gilded Age" resentment. Heitkamp suggests billionaires must change their rhetoric from defensive to collaborative.
* **The "Communist" Label:** Mulvaney characterized Mamdani’s agenda—including government-owned grocery stores—as an experiment in communism that he believes is destined to fail.
* **State-Led Services:** Heitkamp defended the concept of state intervention, citing North Dakota’s state-owned bank and mill as successful examples of government filling gaps where the free enterprise system fails, distinguishing this from "Soviet-style communism."

## Notable Quotes
> "If you go into August to September with $4.50 gallon of gas, it doesn't bode well for the incumbent party. They need this thing to be finished sooner rather than later." — **Mick Mulvaney**

> "We're in a Gilded Age. People are starting to be very resentful of people who aren't taking responsibility but have had tremendous success in this economy." — **Heidi Heitkamp**

> "Maybe Zohran Mamdani is the communist who gets it right... maybe he’s smarter than Lenin and Stalin and Castro and Chavez. My guess is it doesn't [work]." — **Mick Mulvaney**

briefings.title: "Unacceptable": Marco Rubio says Iran must never get nuclear weapons in briefing to media
briefings.tldr: Secretary of State Marco Rubio declared that Iran’s pursuit of nuclear weapons and attempts to control international waterways are "unacceptable," while affirming that the U.S. will maintain a policy of immediate military retaliation against any threats to American personnel or assets.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Secretary of State Marco Rubio declared that Iran’s pursuit of nuclear weapons and attempts to control international waterways are "unacceptable," while affirming that the U.S. will maintain a policy of immediate military retaliation against any threats to American personnel or assets.

## Iran and Global Maritime Security
* **Nuclear Stance:** Rubio emphasized that preventing Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons is a global imperative, noting that while many presidents have stated this, the current administration is taking "concrete" action to prevent it.
* **Negotiation Status:** The U.S. is currently awaiting a response from Tehran regarding a potential negotiation process. Rubio described the Iranian system as "fractured and dysfunctional," which may be delaying the diplomatic timeline.
* **Operation Epic Fury:** Rubio clarified that while the offensive phase of "Operation Epic Fury"—which targeted Iranian missile launchers, naval assets, and factories—is over, the U.S. continues to engage in defensive strikes.
    * **Defensive Retaliation:** Rubio dismissed calls for a ceasefire in the context of self-defense, stating that any drone or missile fired at U.S. destroyers will be met with immediate force.
* **International Waterways:** The Secretary raised alarms over Iran's attempts to "normalize" control over international straits. 
    * **Precedent Risk:** He warned that allowing Iran to control the Strait of Hormuz would set a dangerous precedent for other nations to seize international waterways.
    * **UN Action:** The U.S. is pushing a UN Security Council resolution to condemn the mining and seizing of the straits.

## Diplomatic Relations with the Vatican
* **Cordial Meeting with the Pope:** Despite past friction between the Vatican and the administration, Rubio described his meeting with Pope Leo as "productive" and "very cordial."
* **Strategic Information Exchange:** The briefing focused on the Church’s unique insights into global regions where it has a deep presence, including:
    * **Africa:** Concerns regarding the spread of radical Islamic terrorism threatening growing Christian populations.
    * **Lebanon:** The plight of Christian communities and the role of the Church in facilitating peace.
    * **Venezuela:** Insights from Venezuelan bishops who had recently visited the Vatican.
* **Humanitarian Partnership:** Rubio highlighted the Catholic Church (specifically Caritas) as a vital interlocutor and facilitator for U.S. humanitarian aid in regions where direct government-to-government cooperation is failing.

## U.S. Military Posture and NATO
* **Troop Presence in Europe:** No specific decisions have been made regarding the withdrawal of troops from Italy or a departure from NATO, as these remain presidential prerogatives.
* **Base Usage Concerns:** Rubio expressed frustration with NATO allies (specifically citing Spain) who denied the U.S. use of bases for recent "contingencies." 
    * **Strategic Re-evaluation:** He argued that if NATO bases cannot be used for power projection during emergencies, the U.S. must examine the cost and utility of those deployments.
* **German Deployment:** He clarified that the recent withdrawal of troops from Germany (representing less than 14% of the presence there) was a pre-programmed shift that returned troop levels to 2022 status.

## Regional Policy: Cuba, Lebanon, and Sudan
* **Cuba Sanctions and Aid:** Rubio defended U.S. policy toward Cuba, clarifying that sanctions specifically target **GAESA**, a military-controlled holding company that "steals" from the Cuban people.
    * **Blocked Aid:** He revealed the U.S. offered $100 million in humanitarian aid to Cuba, but the regime has refused to allow its distribution.
* **Lebanon and Hezbollah:** Rubio identified Hezbollah as a "100% Iranian agent" that victimizes the Lebanese people. He called on Italy to help equip the legitimate Lebanese government to confront this threat and cut off illicit financing.
* **Sudan Crisis:** Rubio characterized the war in Sudan as one of the world's worst humanitarian disasters, acting as a proxy war for multiple nations. The U.S. is currently pushing for a "humanitarian ceasefire" and safe haven communities for aid distribution.
* **Taiwan Stability:** Ahead of an upcoming trip to China, Rubio stated that U.S. policy remains unchanged: the U.S. opposes any forced or compelled change to the status quo and advocates for stability in the Taiwan Strait.

## Notable Quotes
> "The red line is clear. If they threaten Americans, they're going to get blown up... Only stupid countries don't shoot back when you're shot at. And we're not a stupid country." — **Marco Rubio**

> "Iran now claims that they own, that they have a right to control an international waterway... if the answer is no, we don't think Iran should be able to control the Strait of Hormuz, then the next question's going to be for everyone: well, what are you going to do about it?" — **Marco Rubio**

> "Our sanctions are against a company named GAESA... This is a holding company set up by generals in Cuba that has generated billions of dollars of revenue, none of which benefits the Cuban people." — **Marco Rubio**

> "I think we all share the same goal, which is a strong Lebanese government that doesn't have an armed Hezbollah operating within its national territory... To do that we have to empower and equip the Lebanese government to be able to confront that threat." — **Marco Rubio**

briefings.title: Watch CNBC's full interview with Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee
briefings.tldr: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee warns that while the labor market remains stable, persistent and rising inflation—particularly in services—is a major concern that may require the Federal Reserve to maintain a restrictive stance and re-evaluate forward guidance.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee warns that while the labor market remains stable, persistent and rising inflation—particularly in services—is a major concern that may require the Federal Reserve to maintain a restrictive stance and re-evaluate forward guidance.

## Labor Market: "Stable Without Being Good"
* **Low-Hire, Low-Fire Environment:** Goolsbee describes the current job market as stagnant rather than deteriorating.
    * **Hiring Rates:** Current hiring levels are comparable to the depths of a recession.
    * **Layoff Rates:** Conversely, layoff rates remain at historic lows typical of an economic boom.
* **Overall Stability:** Despite the "cross-current" in data, Goolsbee notes that unemployment (4.3%) and vacancy rates have remained steady for over a year, suggesting the market is not "falling apart."

## Inflation Concerns and the Dual Mandate
* **The "Wrong Way" Trend:** Goolsbee expressed significant concern that inflation has moved away from the Fed's 2% target over the last three months after five years of being elevated.
* **Service Sector Pressure:** While energy and tariffs contribute to price hikes, Goolsbee highlighted that services inflation is uncomfortably high and not driven by temporary external shocks.
* **Addressing Stagflationary Risks:**
    * **Framework:** In the event of threats to both employment and price stability, the Fed must determine which side is deviating more and the projected duration of that deviation.
    * **Policy Options:** Goolsbee emphasized that "everything should always be on the table," suggesting a stern response might be necessary if inflation expectations become unanchored.

## Monetary Policy and Forward Guidance
* **Skepticism of "Jawboning":** Goolsbee remains skeptical of using forward guidance (words) to influence markets when interest rates are not at the "zero lower bound."
* **The "Data Dog" Approach:** He advocates for a comprehensive review of all economic indicators—including food, energy, and private sector data—rather than focusing strictly on core inflation.
    * **Quote Reference:** He expressed agreement with Chair-designate Kevin Warsh’s view on utilizing a diverse set of inflation measures.

## AI and Productivity Risks
* **Short-Term Overheating:** While AI promises long-term productivity gains, Goolsbee warns against "counting chickens before they hatch."
* **The Wealth Effect:** High expectations for AI can drive up stock market wealth, leading high-end consumers to increase spending before actual economic potential is realized.
* **Supply Chain Bottlenecks:** Massive investment in AI infrastructure is already creating "crowding out" effects, such as:
    * Skyrocketing land prices.
    * Shortages of skilled labor (e.g., electricians).
    * Increased competition for computer chips.

## Notable Quotes

> "I'd characterize it as we've been stable without being good... The hiring rate is low enough it would correspond to kind of the depths of a recession, but at the same time, the layoff rate is as low as would be at the peak of a boom." — **Austan Goolsbee**

> "I want to be one of the data dogs, and one of the main rules of the data dogs is sniff every piece of data that hits the floor because it might be food." — **Austan Goolsbee**

> "Expectations of future productivity growth, the more hyped they are, the more they can contribute to inflation in the short run and they can force the hand of the central bank." — **Austan Goolsbee**

briefings.title: “Weapons of Mass Disruption” with NYT’s Tom Friedman - 05/08/26 | Audio Only
